newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bonds weaken in late trade after solid rally.
newsitem.headline: NZ bonds weaken in late trade after solid rally.

text.p: New Zealand bonds on Friday ended almost unchanged from their Thursday closing levels, but it was a disappointing end to the session after a solid rally earlier in the day, dealers said.

"The market appeared very well bid for most of the afternoon, but I suspect that the volume was a bit on the thin side, and then when someone tried to sell some bonds, it (the bid tone) just evaporated," said one trader.
He said New Zealand debt securities had put in a "quite spectacular" spread performance against the U.S. over the last 24 hours.
"Compared to the close last night we rallied almost ten basis points when the U.S. had sold off five -- that's a 15 point spread contraction on really no news," he said.
"Maybe people had got themselves a little bit short."
While 11/06 bond yields ended at 8.29 percent, below their Thursday closing levels, dealers said they had been as low as 8.24 on the day.
In the short end, 90-day bank bill yields rose two pips to 9.80 percent while the December futures contract softened just a point to 90.75.
Dealers said the debt market would continue to reflect the uncertainties surrounding the outcome of the October 12 general election.

A new opinion poll published by the National Business Review on Friday showed support for the ruling conservative National Party up four points to 38 percent, but support for its potential coalition partner, the free-market Act, fell 0.7 percent to 2.7 percent.
Under the new proportional representation electoral system, parties must breach the 5.0 percent threshold or win an electorate constituency to win seats in parliament.

"I think the market will continue to be very jumpy for the next two or three weeks, in fact maybe the next two months, until the election settles down and until the Reserve Bank actually does something about monetary policy," said a dealer.
